tools.name: listReports
tools.description: The reports the user can see, of every type, newest first. Each report's type tells which endpoints work on it: the slides agent, exports, content, datasheets, parameters, email and ownership transfer take SlideDeck reports only. tools.name: getReport
tools.description: A report of any type with its schedules, who it is shared with and who is emailed when a run fails. lastRunStatus and running tell how its latest run went and whether one is going, and appUrl opens it in Rollstack. type tells which other endpoints work on it.

tools.name: createReport
tools.description: Creates a report of type SlideDeck, in a folder the user can see when folderId is set. It starts empty, or with the look of templateDeckId: its theme, masters and layouts, without its slides. The template must be a SlideDeck report the user may duplicate.

tools.name: updateReport
tools.description: Renames a report of any type, moves it, or changes its timezone or failure notifications. Renaming a report that updates a file, such as a Google Slides presentation, also renames the file, as the app does. Only its editors may.

tools.name: getReportMessage
tools.description: A message to the slides agent and its replies. Waits up to waitSeconds for the message to finish and answers as soon as it does, so call it again while the status is queued or running. A clarification reply asks questions: ask the user, then send the options they pick as answers in a new message on

tools.name: sendReportMessage
tools.description: Asks the slides agent to build or change a report, or to answer a question about it, as the app's chat does. Answers the message's id at once: follow it with getReportMessage. Without chatId the message starts a new chat, which shows in the user's chat history in the app. With it, the message contin

tools.name: approveReportMessageProposal

tools.name: cancelReportMessage
tools.description: Stops a message to the slides agent: a queued one leaves the queue, and a running one stops. A finished one stays as it is. Only the user who sent it may.

tools.name: rejectReportMessageProposal
tools.description: Rejects the proposal of a settings_proposal or email_send_proposal reply, as its Reject button in the app's chat does: nothing changes. Answers the reply with the proposal's status, rejected for a change and cancelled for an email send. Only the user who sent the message may, while they can edit the

tools.name: getReportRun
tools.description: A run's status and the datasheets, or visualizations on a report of another type than SlideDeck, it could not refresh. Waits up to waitSeconds for the run to end and answers as soon as it does, so call it again while the status is running. A user's later run of the report reuses the id, so this desc

tools.description: Refreshes a report's data, or only some of its datasheets, then repairs failed calculations and the slides with AI. tools.name: cancelReportRun
tools.description: Cancels a run of a report, whoever started it. Only its editors may. A run that already ended stays as it is.

tools.name: exportReport
tools.description: Exports a report as PDF or PowerPoint and answers a download link valid for 15 minutes. At most 10 exports a minute per user.

tools.name: getReportContent
tools.description: What a viewer sees on a report's visible slides: titles, text, and each chart's and table's values. On a long report, pass slideIds for only the slides you need, such as a reply's changedSlideIds.

tools.name: getReportSlideImages
tools.description: Renders slides of a report as images, as viewers see them, so you can check how they look: text that overflows or overlaps, or a chart too small to read. After a message's turn, pass its replies' changedSlideIds. At most 10 slides a call; hidden slides are left out. Counts against the 10 exports a m

tools.name: createDataset
tools.description: Stores a CSV for the slides agent to build slides from: a header row, then at least one data row, at most 10 MB. Add it to a report with addReportDatasheets. Over MCP the CSV is written into the tool call, so send large files to this REST endpoint instead. Or send an Excel workbook (.xlsx, at most 1

tools.name: replaceDataset
tools.description: Replaces an uploaded CSV file's rows, or a workbook's content with a new .xlsx sent as multipart/form-data in the file field. It keeps its id, and a CSV is never replaced by a workbook or the other way round. Reports built on it show the new content after their next run or message to the slides agen

tools.name: deleteDataset
tools.description: Deletes an uploaded CSV file or workbook. Reports built on it keep what they last showed, and their datasheets fail on the next read. Only the user who created it may.

tools.name: listReportDatasheets
tools.description: The datasheets a report's charts and tables are built from, with their source and when each was last read.

tools.name: getReportDatasheetData
tools.description: The table a report's chart is drawn from: the datasheet's steps run over the copies stored at its sources' last reads; the source is never queried. tools.name: addReportDatasheets
tools.description: Adds sources to a report as datasheets, and answers their ids in the order of the sources. tools.name: getReportParameters
tools.description: A report's parameters, with which ones a burst can vary by, and the dashboard filters a parameter can link, with the parameter that already links each.

tools.name: createReportParameter
tools.description: Creates a parameter of a report, linked to the dashboard filters given, as the app's report parameters editor does. With a value, writes it into those filters and reads their datasheets again. Answers the parameter. Only the report's editors may.

tools.name: shareReport
tools.description: Shares a report of any type with a member of the organization to view or edit it, or changes their permission. They get an email. A report that updates a file, such as a Google Slides presentation, also shares the file with them, as the app does.

tools.name: unshareReport
tools.description: Removes a user's share of a report of any type, and their access to its file when it updates one, as the app does.

tools.name: updateReportSchedules
tools.description: Replaces the schedules of a report of any type, at most 10; an empty list removes them all. Only its editors may. Every scheduled run updates the whole report: an AI update on a SlideDeck report, and a refresh of every visualization on a report that updates a file. Schedules are checked every 15 min

tools.name: getReportEmailConfig
tools.description: Who a report's email goes to and how it is sent. Answers 404 until its email is set up.

tools.name: updateReportEmailConfig
tools.description: Sets who a report's email goes to and how it is sent, replacing the whole setup. Only its editors may. The sender must be the user's own or shared with the organization.

tools.name: sendReportEmail
tools.description: Emails a report to its recipients now, as it is. Only its editors may. Answers 400 when it has no recipients. Sends in the background; while the user's send of the report is going, starts nothing. At most 5 sends a minute per user, test sends included.

tools.name: sendReportTestEmail
tools.description: Sends a report's email to the user only, and waits until it is sent. Only its editors may. Counts against the 5 sends a minute.

tools.name: listBursts
tools.description: The bursts of reports the user can see, newest first, with the report parameters their variants differ by and the template report they are copied from. tools.name: listBurstVariants
tools.description: A burst's variants the user can open, oldest first, each with its values of the burst's parameters, how its latest run went, whether one is going, and who its email goes to. adding lists the variants the user is still adding. Answers up to limit variants, 50 by default and 200 at most, and a nextCur

tools.name: addBurstVariants

Values are checked first, so a request with one the template's filters can't take adds nothing. Answers at once wi

tools.name: createBurst
tools.description: Makes a report the template of a new burst whose variants differ by the report parameters given, and answers the burst, named after the report and with no variants yet. Add them with addBurstVariants. Only the report's editors may.

tools.name: startBurstRun
tools.description: Starts a run of every variant of a burst, or of the variants passed, as startReportRun does for each: it refreshes the variant's data and repairs its slides with AI. tools.description: Sets who each variant's email goes to, replacing its to, cc and bcc. Its other email settings, such as its sender and which runs send it, stay as copied from the template; a variant without email settings gets the defaults. Sends no email. As in the app, the burst's owner and admins can set any vari

tools.name: removeBurstVariants
tools.description: Removes variants of a burst by their ids, and deletes their reports. Find the ids with listBurstVariants, which shows each variant's parameter values, and confirm them with the user. The user must be able to edit every variant passed, or nothing is removed: the burst's owner and admins can edit them

tools.name: listConnections
tools.description: The data source connections the user can see, without their credentials: each one's type, name, settings such as its URL, owner, admins, default user and whether any user's access works.

tools.name: listSmtpConnections
tools.description: The user's SMTP connections and the ones shared with the organization, without their credentials.

tools.name: listFolders
tools.description: The folders the user can see, each with its parent, null at the top level, and the user's permission on it: null, view, edit or manage. Pass a folder's id as folderId to listReports or createReport.

tools.description: The members of the organization, with their role, authentication role, insights access and whether they are active. Optionally only those with a status, active or deactivated, or with an email.

findings.detail: Description of "searchDashboards" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: getReportMessage, getReportSlideImages, shareReport, listBurstVariants, submitFeedback · Private data: updateReport, startReportRun, createDataset, replaceDataset, deleteDataset, getReportDatasheetData, addReportDatasheets, shareReport, unshareReport, updateReportSchedules, listConnections, searchSpreadsheets, getSpreadsheet, listSmtpConnections · Public sink: listReports, getReportMessage, sendReportMessage, approveReportMessageProposal, rejectReportMessageProposal, startReportRun, createDataset, shareReport, unshareReport, getReportEmailConfig, updateReportEmailConfig, sendReportEmail, sendReportTestEmail, listBurstVariants, updateBurstVariantRecipients, submitFeedback, listMembers · Destructive: getReport, getReportRun, startReportRun, cancelReportRun, replaceDataset, getReportDatasheetData, addReportDatasheets, updateReportSchedules, listBurstVariants, startBurstRun.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: getReportMessage, getReportSlideImages, shareReport, listBurstVariants, submitFeedback · Private data: updateReport, startReportRun, createDataset, replaceDataset, deleteDataset, getReportDatasheetData, addReportDatasheets, shareReport, unshareReport, updateReportSchedules, listConnections, searchSpreadsheets, getSpreadsheet, listSmtpConnections · Public sink: listReports, getReportMessage, sendReportMessage, approveReportMessageProposal, rejectReportMessageProposal, startReportRun, createDataset, shareReport, unshareReport, getReportEmailConfig, updateReportEmailConfig, sendReportEmail, sendReportTestEmail, listBurstVariants, updateBurstVariantRecipients, submitFeedback, listMembers · Destructive: getReport, getReportRun, startReportRun, cancelReportRun, replaceDataset, getReportDatasheetData, addReportDatasheets, updateReportSchedules, listBurstVariants, startBurstRun

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
